Vaslav Nijinsky was a Russian dancer and choreographer of unparalleled technical virtuosity and artistic daring whose brief but revolutionary career redefined what the male dancer could express and accomplish. Rising to stardom with the Ballets Russes under Sergei Diaghilev, he became a legendary performer and created controversial choreography that challenged classical ballet's formal conventions. Though his creative period lasted only a few years before mental illness curtailed his work, his influence on modern dance and ballet aesthetics remains immeasurable.

He was born in eighteen eighty-nine in Kiev. He trained at the Imperial Ballet School in St. Petersburg, where he became the protégé of Sergei Diaghilev. He joined the Ballets Russes in nineteen oh nine as its principal dancer and quickly became the company's superstar. He was known for extraordinary elevation, speed, and an androgynous stage presence that captivated European audiences.

He performed principal roles in Michel Fokine choreography including The Firebird in nineteen ten and Petrushka in nineteen eleven. Through these performances, he became the dancer through whom Fokine's revolutionary vision was realized. His technical abilities were legendary and his artistry unmatched.

He then turned to choreography. He choreographed L'Après-midi d'un faune in nineteen twelve, a controversial work of deliberate earthiness and sexuality that shocked conservative audiences. This marked the beginning of his career as an innovator. He created The Rite of Spring in nineteen thirteen, setting it to Stravinsky's revolutionary score. His choreography presaged modernism and modern dance. The premiere sparked a famous riot in Paris due to its radical rejection of classical ballet conventions.

His choreography emphasized angularity, ground-based movement, and psychological intensity—a stark departure from Petipa's verticality and ethereal aesthetics. He revolutionized the role of the male dancer, transforming it from supporting partner to commanding virtuoso and artist-creator.

He suffered a mental health crisis in nineteen seventeen, spending much of his remaining life institutionalized. He died in nineteen fifty, leaving a body of work smaller than his legend. Yet what he created changed dance forever.

The Ballets Russes is the company through which he achieved stardom and created his revolutionary works. Michel Fokine is the choreographer whose works he premiered with legendary artistry. Igor Stravinsky was his compositional partner on The Rite of Spring, a paradigm-shifting collaboration. The Rite of Spring is his most famous choreographic creation, a modernist masterpiece. Sergei Diaghilev was the impresario who discovered him and championed his artistic vision. Modernism is the artistic movement his work embodied and advanced. Modern dance is connected to his choreographic innovations, which helped bridge classical ballet and the emerging modern dance aesthetic.
